title: Cap. X Arg. I close: Augustine — God can convert any wills; he eternally established to do so in some, not in others, by mere good pleasure; Vasquez — rejection from grace has no cause in the rejected beyond first parents' sin
pass_a_gloss: For He who can, as Augustine speaks, De bono persever. cap. 8. convert the averse and adverse wills of any whomsoever, and from eternity established to do this in certain ones, in certain ones not to do it, he elects and passes over, has mercy and has not mercy, not according to a foreknown difference of human wills, but according to the mere good pleasure of his will. Now let Vasquez be heard: If reprobation be used for the act whereby someone is rejected by God, either we speak of the act whereby someone is rejected from the grace of God, or whereby he is rejected from the kingdom of the heavens. If the discourse be of the former, it is to be asserted that no cause is given on the part of him who is rejected, beyond the sin of the first parent, In 1. disp. 89. c. 5. p. 701. Although therefore no one is excluded from heaven and sent away unto gehenna from the sentence of God judging, except on account of his own sins: yet, even this Jesuit freely confessing, all the reprobate are rejected from the grace of the predestined from the liberty of God, doing of his own what he wills.
pass_b_english: For he who can — as Augustine says (De bono persever. cap. 8) — convert anyone's averse and adverse wills, and from eternity established to do this in some and not in others, elects and passes over, has mercy and has not mercy, not by a foreknown difference of human wills, but by the mere good pleasure of his will. Hear Vasquez: If reprobation is used for the act whereby someone is rejected by God, we speak either of rejection from God's grace, or of rejection from the kingdom of heaven. If of the former, it must be asserted that no cause is given on the rejected one's part beyond the first parent's sin (In 1. disp. 89. c. 5. p. 701). So although no one is shut out of heaven and sent to gehenna by God's judging sentence except for his own sins — yet, even this Jesuit freely confessing, all the reprobate are rejected from the predestined's grace by God's liberty, doing of his own what he wills.
source_text: Nam Qui potest, ut loquitur Augustinus, De bono persever. cap. 8. aversas et adversas quorumvis convertere voluntates, et hoc ab aeterno statuit in quibusdam facere, in quibusdam non facere, ille non secundum praescitam differentiam humanarum voluntatum, sed secundum merum beneplacitum suae voluntatis, eligit et praeterit, miseretur et non miseretur. Jam Vasques audiatur: Si reprobatio usurpetur pro actu quo quis rejicitur a Deo, aut loquimur de actu quo quis rejicitur a gratia Dei, aut quo rejicitur a regno caelorum. Si de priore sermo sit, asserendum est nullam causam ex parte ejus dari qui rejicitur, praeter peccatum primi parentis, In 1. disp. 89. c. 5. p. 701. Quamvis igitur nemo e caelo excludatur et in gehennam ablegetur ex sententia Dei judicantis, nisi propter peccata propria: tamen, vel hoc Jesuita ultro confitente, omnes reprobati rejiciuntur a gratia praedestinatorum ex libertate Dei, de suo quod vult facientis.
